To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of roasted soybeans or blood meal as a source of fat and rup in lactating cow diets did not affect milk production and composition.
the inclusion of blood meal or roasted soybeans in the diets of high producing lactating cows did not affect milk yield but reduced milk protein content and DMI.

1) roasted soybeans can be used as an alternative to soybean meal for high yielding cows, 2) ground roasted soybean diets can be fed at a higher level (18%) without affecting milk fat or milk protein percentage, and 3) blood meal diets should be fed at a lower level than soybean meal diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of roasted soybean meal, blood meal, tallow, and combinations thereof on milk production and composition.
the use of blood meal and roasted soybeans as sources of fat, protein, and energy in diets for lactating cows.
the use of blood meal as a source of RUP in dairy rations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
roasted soybeans and blood meal can be used as sources of RUP and fat in lactating dairy cow rations.
roasted soybeans are a suitable source of protein for lactating dairy cattle.

blood meal and tallow, roasted soybean diets are comparable with soybean meal diets in terms of milk yield and composition, and blood meal and roasted soybean diets result in reduced DMI and milk protein percentage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
roasted soybeans are an acceptable source of fat and RDP in diets for lactating cows.

the use of roasted soybean meal and blood meal in high yielding lactating cows is feasible and that roasted soybean meal can be fed as a substitute for soybean meal without any adverse effect on milk production.
the inclusion of roasted soybeans or blood meal in the diets of cows did not affect milk yield or milk fat content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
blood meal and whole or ground roasted soybean diets were not as effective as soybean meal in supporting high milk yields.
blood meal can be used as a source of ruminally undigested protein and fat in diets fed to lactating dairy cows.

the inclusion of roasted soybeans and blood meal in the diets of high producing dairy cows did not affect the milk fat percentage, and that roasted soybeans and whole soybeans are good substitutes for blood meal in high producing lactating dairy cows.
